written:
## 1. The numbers
Risk-off. A tech rout hit global markets and pushed US stocks toward their longest losing streak since 2020, while investors moved into bonds. Volatility jumped and Bitcoin fell with equities.

## 2. What moved and why
**AI trade unravels, dragging the Nasdaq lower**
Why it happened: Worries that the AI trade is coming apart set off a rush out of riskier assets worldwide. Anthropic's 11% drop on its second trading day typifies the shift in mood.
Why it matters: The Nasdaq is now negative for 2026, and the weakness is spreading to chips and Asian tech.

**Gold slides to 14-month lows on rate-hike fears**
Why it happened: Fed officials signalled openness to more rate hikes, and investors sold metals to cover losses from the AI stock rout.
Why it matters: Higher yields and a stronger dollar make non-yielding gold less attractive, and the slide hurts gold holders and miners.

**Quebecor, Telus and BCE spark a telecom bidding fight**
Why it happened: Quebecor proposed acquiring rival Telus in a deal that could reshape Canada's telecom industry. Reports then emerged that BCE had entered talks with Telus to explore its options.
Why it matters: A Canadian telecom merger would change competition and pricing, and it would draw close regulatory attention.

## Deals
- **Acquisition: Quebecor → Telus** (About $31.3B proposed value). Unsolicited, not a signed deal. Quebecor wants to combine two major Canadian carriers, and BCE has reportedly entered the picture.
- **Acquisition: Canadian Natural Resources → Advantage Energy** (About $2.53B total transaction value). It adds Montney and Charlie Lake assets next to existing operations.
- **Acquisition: Bending Spoons → Mailchimp (from Intuit)** ($3.68B enterprise value, plus a $1.30B share sale). It buys an established email-marketing platform.

## 3. What's coming today
- Today, at the close: Monthly options expiration. It can amplify swings after a week of heavy selling.
- Today 3:30 PM: CFTC positioning data on gold.

## 4. Canada corner
- Quebecor plunged more than 15% to $65.25, the worst performer on the TSX that day. Telus climbed nearly 14%.
- Telecoms offered a modest rebound on Bay Street today even as AI-linked stocks fell.
- The TSX has a large gold-mining weighting, so gold holders and miners are exposed.

## 5. The takeaway
Risk-off moves can spread fast: when a crowded theme such as AI unwinds, forced selling hits unrelated assets like gold too.

data.headline: AI selloff deepens as Anthropic slides, gold sinks
data.mood: Risk-off. A tech rout hit global markets and pushed US stocks toward their longest losing streak since 2020, while investors moved into bonds. Volatility jumped and Bitcoin fell with equities.

stories.title: AI trade unravels, dragging the Nasdaq lower
stories.why_happened: Worries that the AI trade is coming apart set off a rush out of riskier assets worldwide. Anthropic's 11% drop on its second trading day typifies the shift in mood.
stories.why_matters: The Nasdaq is now negative for 2026, and the weakness is spreading to chips and Asian tech.
stories.full: The AI boom has carried markets for months, and that support is weakening. The Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026 even though Anthropic's IPO and Nvidia's earnings were supposed to help. The S&P 500 was set for a seventh straight decline. Thursday's damage was already large. The S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7,175.83 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.25% to 23,879.20. Anthropic gained 17% on its first day, but it then reversed by more than 10%. The selloff spread to Asia. SoftBank dropped over 16%, and SK Hynix and Samsung fell 6% and 4.7%. Defensive areas held up better. The Dow was lifted by healthcare names such as UnitedHealth and by Walmart. Taiwan stocks were heading for their worst weekly drop in nearly three decades. Watch whether the losing streak extends, how chip stocks trade into today's close, and whether the dollar keeps rising. The dollar index was near a 19-month high and set for a fourth weekly gain.

stories.title: Gold slides to 14-month lows on rate-hike fears
stories.why_happened: Fed officials signalled openness to more rate hikes, and investors sold metals to cover losses from the AI stock rout.
stories.why_matters: Higher yields and a stronger dollar make non-yielding gold less attractive, and the slide hurts gold holders and miners.
stories.full: Gold has had a rough year. It set a record of $5,589.38 in January and fell below $3,800 on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025. It dropped to about $3,548 today, a 14-month low, and is on course for its worst week in eight months. The driver is rates. The dollar strengthened toward a 19-month high while Treasury yields stayed elevated, so interest-bearing assets compete better with gold. The World Gold Council points to stronger inflation data and hawkish Fed comments raising the odds of another hike. Forced selling added to the move, as funds sold metals to meet equity losses. Gold holders and gold miners are the losers. Canadian investors should note that the TSX has a large gold-mining weighting. Not everyone has turned bearish. Morgan Stanley still named gold its top commodity pick for 2027. Watch the $3,500 level. It is the next widely watched psychological threshold. Further Fed comments will matter too.

stories.title: Quebecor, Telus and BCE spark a telecom bidding fight
stories.why_happened: Quebecor proposed acquiring rival Telus in a deal that could reshape Canada's telecom industry. Reports then emerged that BCE had entered talks with Telus to explore its options.
stories.why_matters: A Canadian telecom merger would change competition and pricing, and it would draw close regulatory attention.
stories.full: Quebecor's unsolicited proposal valued Telus at roughly $31.3 billion, and a Nov. 18 Globe and Mail report said BCE was interested while Telus was already weighing the offer. The market reacted sharply. Quebecor plunged more than 15% to $65.25, the worst performer on the TSX that day. Telus climbed nearly 14%. Telus shareholders benefit from the prospect of competing bids. Quebecor's drop suggests investors doubt the price or how it would be financed. Quebecor defended its proposal and plans to meet Telus management on November 23. Telecoms offered a modest rebound on Bay Street today even as AI-linked stocks fell. Watch for formal offers, any counterbid from BCE, and how regulators view a combination of national carriers.

deals.why: Unsolicited, not a signed deal. Quebecor wants to combine two major Canadian carriers, and BCE has reportedly entered the picture.
deals.full: The proposal valued Telus at roughly $31.3 billion. Telus is evaluating it, and Quebecor will meet management on November 23. No definitive agreement exists yet. The logic is consolidation. Quebecor would gain scale against the other national carriers. The share reaction shows the market likes the price for Telus but doubts the benefit for Quebecor. The signal is that Canadian telecom is in play, and BCE's reported interest could turn this into a contested situation. Expect heavy regulatory scrutiny of any outcome.

deals.why: It adds Montney and Charlie Lake assets next to existing operations.
deals.full: Canadian Natural will pay $13.55 per share in cash, about $2.255 billion in equity value, or about $2.53 billion including net debt and convertible debentures. That price is a 25% premium to the November 13 close. It will be funded from cash and existing bank credit facilities. The deal adds Montney and Charlie Lake production near Canadian Natural's Grande Prairie operations, and the company expects efficiencies of scale in the area. It signals continued consolidation among Canadian producers, funded with cash rather than shares.

deals.value: $3.68B enterprise value, plus a $1.30B share sale
deals.why: It buys an established email-marketing platform.
deals.full: Bending Spoons agreed to acquire Mailchimp from Intuit at an enterprise value of $3.68 billion. The same day it agreed to sell 32.5 million shares to institutional investors for expected gross proceeds of $1.30 billion. Closing is expected in early 2027. The sources I found don't give a valuation multiple or say how the proceeds will be used. The pairing suggests the share sale helps fund the purchase, though that is an inference. For Intuit, it is a portfolio disposal.
